To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the survival signal-related proteins, phosphatidyinositol 3kinase and Akt, decrease in the early and symptomatic stage of transgenic mice with mutant SOD1, which may contribute to subsequent motor neuronal loss.
the majority of the spinal motor neurons lost immunoreactivities for PI3-K and for Akt in the early stage of the transgenic mouse model of ALS.
the early decrease of survival signaling proteins in the spinal cord may be a critical event for the pathogenesis of motor neuronal death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early decrease of survival signals in motor neurons of transgenic mice expressing a mutant SOD gene.
the mechanisms of motor neuronal loss in the transgenic mice with mutant SOD1, which may be relevant to those in human ALS.
the molecular mechanisms of the motor neuronal loss in ALS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PI3K and Akt are involved in the survival and/or maintenance of the motor neuron pool in the spinal cord.
the early decrease of survival signaling in the spinal motor neuron may be a critical event in the development of ALS.
a decrease in the survival signals in motor neurons may be one of the mechanisms of the neuronal death in ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the survival signal pathway is downregulated in presymptomatic ALS mice.
the motor neuronal loss in ALS is not due to the oxidative stress, but rather to the failure in neuronal survival signaling.
an early and presymptive decrease in the survival signal-related protein expression is a common phenomenon for motor neurons in both the human ALS and the transgenic animal model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early decrease of survival signals in the presymptomatic motor neurons may be involved in the pathogenesis of motor neuronal loss in the transgenic mice with the mutant SOD1.

the majority of motor neurons in the early presymptomatic phase of the transgenic mouse model of ALS lose the immunoreactivities of PI3-K, Akt, and p70S6K, which are involved in the survival signal pathway.

we found that the majority of motor neurons lose the immunoreactivities of PI3-K/Akt in presymptomatic stages of the mutant SOD1 mouse model, and that this decrease may contribute to the subsequent motor neuron degeneration.
